title: Pal_finder Protocol for Sequence Analysis
author: Ruth Madrigal-Brenes
materials: Upload the raw sequences of each individual.
Submodule and limit specifying file : None.
Paste Customized adapter sequences in FASTA format.
Always keep both reads (PE specific/palindrome mode)? Yes
Mispriming library to use : Default from pal_finder
Download the output file named: MiMi_output_all_loci

steps.title: Check sequences with FastQC
steps.instruction: Perform sequence quality control using FastQC.

substeps.instruction: Select raw sequences for Short read data, processing Forward (R1) and Reverse (R2) separately for each individual.
Upload a text file (.txt) containing adapter names and sequences to the Adapter list.

steps.title: Clean sequences using Trimmomatic-Galaxy
steps.instruction: Clean sequences using Trimmomatic-Galaxy Version 0.38.1 with specific configuration settings.

substeps.instruction: Set 'Disable grouping of bases for reads >50 bp' to None.
Leave 'Lower limit on sequence length' as the default setting (blank).
Select 'paired-end' for 'Single-end or paired-end reads?' (using two separate input files).
Set 'Perform initial ILLUMINACLIP step?' to Yes.
Select 'Custom' for 'Select standard adapter sequences or provide custom?'.
Set 'Maximum mismatch count which will still allow a full match to be performed' to 2.
Set the accuracy for the match between the two 'adapter ligated' reads for PE palindrome read alignment to 30.
Set the accuracy for the match between any adapter etc. sequence against a read to 10.
Set 'Minimum length of adapter that needs to be detected (PE specific/palindrome mode)' to 8.

steps.title: Run pal_finder in Galaxy
steps.instruction: Execute pal_finder on the Galaxy server using the following parameters.

substeps.instruction: Enter a text prefix in 'Primer prefix' to identify each individual.
Select 'Illumina' for 'Sequencing platform used to generate data'.
Choose 'Pair of datasets' for 'Input Type' and select the paired sequences obtained from Trimmomatic.
Set 'Use all reads for microsatellite detection?' to Yes.
Select all default options for 'Filters to apply to the pal_finder results'.
Set 'Use PANDAseq to assemble paired-end reads and confirm primer sequences are present in high-quality assembly' to Yes.
Set 'Minimum number of 2-mer repeat units to detect' to 6.
Set 'Minimum number of 4-mer, 5-mer, and 6-mer repeat units' to 3.
Use default 'Primer settings' from pal_finder, but set the GC percentage range to 40–60%.

steps.title: Prepare HPC Cluster Environment
steps.instruction: Set up the computational environment on an HPC cluster.

substeps.instruction: Create a user account on an HPC cluster and ensure approximately 100 GB of storage space.
Load necessary modules: Biopython, PANDAseq, MUSCLE, and MiMi.
Upload and decompress the cleaned sequences for each individual on the HPC cluster.

steps.title: Configure and Run MiMi
steps.instruction: Configure and execute the MiMi program.

substeps.instruction: Edit the MiMi configuration file to adjust paths to the MiMi program location and the uploaded cleaned sequences.
Run MiMi using the command: python MiMi_v0.1.2.py -c 'path to configuration file'

steps.title: Analyze and Filter MiMi Results
steps.instruction: Process the MiMi output to identify polymorphic microsatellites.

substeps.instruction: Open the file 'MiMi_output_all_loci' using spreadsheet software.
Filter out monomorphic microsatellites by selecting the 'Size_Range' column for values greater than 0.

Filter potential polymorphic microsatellites to those present in at least 6 of the 8 analyzed individuals (75%) by selecting the 'Samples_containing_raw_reads_(respectively)' column for 6 or more samples.
Filter for an allelic richness of Ar = 3 or higher by selecting the 'Alleles_present' column for three or more alleles.
